## Steps

1. `list_available_experiments` — Need doses and replicates to plan discriminating wells.

8. `submit_conclusion` — Enlarged single round nuclei with high integrated DNA and atlas match to DNA-damage agents.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 7: DNA damage 0.65, DNA replication 0.25, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.10

## Conclusion

**DNA damage** (stated probability 0.65); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e5.

Why: Enlarged single round nuclei with high integrated DNA and atlas match to DNA-damage agents.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Stain for gamma-H2AX foci and phospho-ATM plus flow-cytometry cell-cycle to confirm DNA-damage G2 arrest vs replication stress; compare to mitomycin C control.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean profile, no hidden confounder, probability calibrated.

## Unblinding

Compound: **etoposide** (PubChem CID [36462](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/36462))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **DNA damage**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The call was driven by very large, replicated nuclear effects: nuc_area z=+18.1 at 10 uM and z=+12.2 at 1 uM with high frac_large_nucleus z=+18.6 and increased integrated DNA content, plus lower density microscopically. Atlas comparison favoring DNA damage 5/10 over DNA replication 4/10 correctly tipped the balance, and unblinding to etoposide as a topoisomerase II inhibitor (PMID 16101488, PMID 42442624) validated that weighting.

The main weakness was discrimination power: DNA damage vs DNA replication was close in the atlas, which is biologically expected because topoisomerase II poisons also inhibit replication (PMID 35578785). I acquired only the two available wells, so dose_response failed for lack of a third well and I could not demonstrate a dose trend, and the second literature search on phenotype was too narrow and returned 0 hits.

Probability 0.65 for DNA damage was appropriately cautious rather than overconfident. Aurora kinase was correctly downweighted because the phenotype was enlarged single nuclei with high DNA content rather than clear multinucleation, but a mitotic marker would have made that exclusion stronger.

What was right:
- Flagged massive nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z +12 to +18, frac_large_nucleus z +18.6) across two doses as G2/DNA-damage arrest signal
- Used increased nuc_dna_integrated z +7 to +10 to support DNA accumulation rather than mitotic fragmentation
- Followed compare_to_reference_atlas majority (DNA damage 5/10) while retaining DNA replication as runner-up, matching topoisomerase II biology
- Correctly downweighted Aurora kinase inhibitors despite 1/10 hit because visual phenotype lacked multinucleation

What was wrong or missed:
- Acquired only 2 wells total, so dose_response tool failed and no 3-point dose trend could be established
- Did not resolve DNA damage vs DNA replication mechanistically; 4/10 replication hits were noted but not tested
- Second literature search was too specific ('etoposide nuclear enlargement G2 arrest MCF-7 phenotype') and returned 0 hits instead of broadening query

Proposed next experiment: Stain treated MCF-7 cells for gamma-H2AX and phospho-ATM with DNA-content flow cytometry to confirm DNA-break foci and G2 arrest, comparing etoposide to a DNA replication-stress control to separate damage from replication inhibition.

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [16101488](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16101488/): Etoposide, topoisomerase II and cancer. *Curr Med Chem Anticancer Agents* (2005) — Etoposide acts as a topoisomerase II poison that generates DNA damage.
- PMID [35578785](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35578785/): Topoisomerase II poisons inhibit vertebrate DNA replication through distinct mechanisms. *EMBO J* (2022) — Topoisomerase II poisons also inhibit vertebrate DNA replication, which explains the atlas overlap between DNA damage and replication signatures.
- PMID [42442624](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42442624/): Targeting DNA topoisomerase II in Cancer: mechanism of inhibition, clinical utility, and future directions. *Gene* (2026) — Inhibition of DNA topoisomerase II is an established DNA-damaging mechanism in cancer biology.
